payload.last_agent_message:
I’d hold this migration until the existing column definition and deployment plan are checked.

- **[P1] The type change can block writes for the duration of a table copy** — [input-3.sql:2](C:/Users/Gary/AppData/Local/Temp/day10-review-_6wfhepa/baseline/input-3.sql:2). If `shipment_seq` is currently a different type, MySQL 8.0 must copy and rebuild the table to change it to `BIGINT`; concurrent DML is not permitted during that operation. On 20 million rows, this could cause a prolonged write outage and requires substantial extra disk space. Use a tested online schema-change approach if writes must remain available, or schedule and rehearse a maintenance window. [MySQL online DDL documentation](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-online-ddl-operations.html)

- **[P1] The column definition may change more than its type** — [input-3.sql:2](C:/Users/Gary/AppData/Local/Temp/day10-review-_6wfhepa/baseline/input-3.sql:2). `MODIFY` supplies the new definition: this statement makes the column signed and `NOT NULL`, and may remove existing attributes such as its default. Existing `NULL` values can cause the migration to fail or be converted depending on SQL mode. Check `SHOW CREATE TABLE orders`, preserve intended attributes, and backfill and prevent new nulls before enforcing `NOT NULL`. [MySQL ALTER TABLE documentation](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/alter-table.html)

The index addition on [line 3](C:/Users/Gary/AppData/Local/Temp/day10-review-_6wfhepa/baseline/input-3.sql:3) can normally run concurrently with reads and writes, though it still needs metadata locks. Consider explicitly specifying `ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE` so it fails rather than accepting a more disruptive operation, and check whether an existing index already covers `customer_id`. The two statements are separate DDL operations, so plan recovery for the case where the column change succeeds and the index creation fails.

The current schema and data weren’t included, so I couldn’t verify whether the conditional column risks apply or run the migration against representative data.
